# autter_alert_rule (Resource)

An alert rule of a repository: which runtime issue events reach whom. Addressed by its name within the repository.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "autter_repository" "web" {
  full_name = "acme/web"
}

resource "autter_alert_rule" "checkout_errors" {
  repository_id = data.autter_repository.web.id
  name          = "Checkout errors"
  triggers      = ["new", "regressed", "spiking"]

  filters = {
    environments = ["production"]
    services     = ["checkout", "payments"]
    priorities   = ["p0", "p1"]
    message = {
      op    = "contains"
      value = "Timeout"
    }
    threshold = {
      min_events     = 5
      window_minutes = 30
    }
  }

  actions = {
    # {} posts to the repository's Slack route; set channel_id for another channel.
    slack = {}
    email = {
      assignee = true
      watchers = true
    }
    oncall = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `actions` (Attributes) Where the alert goes. At least one of `slack`, `email`, `in_app` or `oncall = true`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions))
- `name` (String) The alert rule's name, unique in the repository: the API addresses it by name. Changing it replaces the resource (a rename is a delete and a create). If a alert rule with this name already exists, it is adopted.
- `repository_id` (String) The repository: its id, usually `data.autter_repository.<label>.id`. Its full name (`owner/repo`) also works, but after an import the id is stored, so use the id to keep plans clean. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `triggers` (List of String) The issue events the rule fires on: `new`, `regressed`, `spiking`, `assigned`, `resolved`.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule fires. Default `true`.
- `filters` (Attributes) Which issues the rule applies to. Left out: every issue. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the alert rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `created_by` (String) The id of the member who created the alert rule; null for one Autter created.
- `id` (String) The alert rule's id in Autter. Informational: the provider addresses it by repository and name.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is one of the rules a repository starts with.
- `updated_at` (String) When the alert rule was last changed (ISO 8601). It does not move when an apply changes nothing.

<a id="nestedatt--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions`

Optional:

- `auto_assignments` (Boolean) Also send automatic assignments to Slack and on-call.
- `email` (Attributes) A line in each recipient's daily update summary. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--email))
- `in_app` (Attributes) An in-app notification. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--in_app))
- `oncall` (Boolean) Page on-call when the issue is critical (p0, or a fatal error).
- `slack` (Attributes) Post to Slack. `slack = {}` uses the repository's Slack route. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--actions--slack))

<a id="nestedatt--actions--email"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions.email`

Optional:

- `assignee` (Boolean) The issue's assignee.
- `everyone` (Boolean) Every member of the organization.
- `user_ids` (List of String) These members, by user id.
- `watchers` (Boolean) The issue's assignee and every member who assigned, resolved, ignored or reopened it.


<a id="nestedatt--actions--in_app"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions.in_app`

Optional:

- `assignee` (Boolean) The issue's assignee.
- `everyone` (Boolean) Every member of the organization.
- `user_ids` (List of String) These members, by user id.
- `watchers` (Boolean) The issue's assignee and every member who assigned, resolved, ignored or reopened it.


<a id="nestedatt--actions--slack"></a>
### Nested Schema for `actions.slack`

Optional:

- `channel_id` (String) A Slack channel id; left out: the repository's Slack route.



<a id="nestedatt--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters`

Optional:

- `assignee` (String) `any` (the default), `assigned`, `unassigned`, `me` (the rule's author) or `user:<id>`.
- `environments` (List of String) Environments; empty or left out: any environment.
- `error_type` (Attributes) Match the issue's error type. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--error_type))
- `levels` (List of String) Issue levels, for example `fatal`, `error`, `warning`.
- `message` (Attributes) Match the issue's message, or its title when it has none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--message))
- `priorities` (List of String) Priorities: `p0` to `p3`, or `none` for an issue not ranked yet.
- `services` (List of String) Services; empty or left out: any service.
- `threshold` (Attributes) Alert only once the issue has at least this many events or users within the window. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--threshold))

<a id="nestedatt--filters--error_type"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters.error_type`

Required:

- `op` (String) How to match: `equals`, `contains`, `starts_with` or `regex`.
- `value` (String) The text or pattern, up to 200 characters.


<a id="nestedatt--filters--message"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters.message`

Required:

- `op` (String) How to match: `equals`, `contains`, `starts_with` or `regex`.
- `value` (String) The text or pattern, up to 200 characters.


<a id="nestedatt--filters--threshold"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters.threshold`

Optional:

- `min_events` (Number) Minimum events.
- `min_users` (Number) Minimum users.
- `window_minutes` (Number) The window in minutes, up to 10080 (7 days). The API's default is 60.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = autter_alert_rule.checkout_errors
  id = "acme/web:Checkout errors"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is "<repository>:<name>": the repository's id or owner/repo, then
# the rule's name (which may itself contain colons).
terraform import autter_alert_rule.checkout_errors "acme/web:Checkout errors"
```
